answer: Grading seats are held at a self-assessed value with a weekly tax, and anyone may buy a seat at its stated value, so a farm hoarding seats pays rent forever or loses them to buyers. A farm holding a hundred grading seats pays a hundred weekly taxes, and underpricing them invites a buyout, while one honest grader holds one seat fairly. The raven of the design is public, the nebula of stakes makes farming a losing trade, and the forge of honest work is what finally pays.
